title: Component study: first combination holds on two seeds.
text: The per-variable loss, per-modality weights and attention gate together, against the control of the same seed at 8,000 steps: overall CRPS -1.0% and -1.9%, NEE -3.1% and -1.5%, LE -2.2% and -2.5%, H -2.8% and -2.4%, FCH4 -18.1% and -15.5%, with 95% coverage 0.953 and 0.954. All four fluxes gain on both seeds, and the FCH4 instability of per-modality weights alone is gone. The combination is adopted. Solar geometry and the weight EMA show no gain. Combinations with SwiGLU and the quantile head are running.

title: Deep ensemble on all test windows.
text: The per-tower deep ensemble of Vekuri et al. (2025) finished all 514 test windows and joins the test tables. Its CRPS on matched cells is 2.015 for NEE, 21.04 for LE, 27.19 for H and 30.85 for FCH4, so the margins of FluxFill do not change: NEE 14.2%, LE 17.7%, H 18.1% and FCH4 3.6% lower than the best other method. By gap, FluxFill now has the lowest CRPS in 26 of 44 flux and gap combinations, Chronos-2 in 8, XGBoost in 5, the deep ensemble in 3 and the random forest ensemble in 2. The deep ensemble takes the mixed per-variable family M5 on NEE, LE and H.

title: Component study: second seeds.
text: The per-variable loss of 4M lowers FCH4 CRPS by 16.9% and 15.1% on two seeds, and the attention gate of Timestral lowers overall CRPS by 1.5% on both; both enter the next model. Per-modality weights lower overall CRPS by 1.3% on both seeds, but FCH4 moves from -4.9% to +26.3%, so the combination runs decide. The quantile head (FCH4 -19.9%) and SwiGLU (overall CRPS -2.8%) wait for second seeds. Asinh scaling and the FGN loss are rejected.

title: Chronos-2 on the test towers.
text: Chronos-2 finished the 514 test windows on families M2, M3 and M4. FluxFill keeps the lowest pooled CRPS on all four fluxes. By gap, Chronos-2 leads LE at 2 and 6 hours, H at 6 hours, and FCH4 at 2 and 6 hours, 1 and 30 days and real outages. CSDI was stopped at 21 test windows: at 1.5 hours per window the full set would take about 31 days. Chronos-2 forecasts diverge on 11 of the 514 windows; they stay in its scores and the Test note gives its CRPS without them.

title: Component study.
text: One change at a time against a control, with the published form of each technique. Results appear in the Results tab and in report Table 4 as each run finishes. Rows are provisional until they hold on a second seed.

title: Temporal copula adopted.
text: Refitted on the final model without site adaptation. On 50 validation windows the 95% coverage of 30-day sums rises from 0.363 to 0.960 and of window sums from 0.361 to 0.965, the CRPS of those sums falls by 18.6% and 18.9%, and the CRPS of half-hourly values does not change. The fit used the same windows; the final test scoring measures the gain.

title: Methane validation towers.
text: 13 spatial blocks of training towers (21 towers, 13 measuring methane) moved to validation, drawn to match the ecosystem mix of the methane test towers. Methane towers are now 82 training, 18 validation and 21 test; the test towers are unchanged. Validation gains 102 methane windows. A model trained on this split is in training.

title: Longer training.
text: A run of 48,000 steps reached validation CRPS 0.1612 at step 40,000, 2.6% below the 0.1655 of the current 24,000-step model.

title: Test baselines.
text: XGBoost, the random forest ensemble and SAITS were scored on all 514 test windows and added to the test results.

title: Tower pages.
text: 795 of 823 towers on the Towers tab link to their AmeriFlux (401), ICOS (363) or FLUXNET (31) site pages.
